clue.text: Enigmatic work, equal tempered apart from fourth in scale

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work

indicators.note: tempered suggests something modified or worked over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
apart from means the named letter is excluded from the word equal
fourth in points to the letter in fourth position of the word scale

explanation.surface: A musician describes a puzzling piece written in equal temperament, except for one note of the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equal tempered' looks like the musical tuning system, but 'tempered' is the anagram signal; 'fourth in scale' is a letter of that word, not a musical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to see through or understand is called obscure, a common figurative synonym.

clue.text: More than one pancake roll for the northern girl to tuck into

indicators.note: to tuck into means the following pieces go inside the word for roll

parts.note: to toss is to roll or throw about
T' is the northern English dialect form of the
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A northern girl is offered a pancake roll to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire and other northern English dialects 'the' is shortened to T'. 'More than one' signals a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Tostadas are crisp fried Mexican tortillas, flat corn breads akin to a pancake, plural here.

clue.text: Youth exchanging knight for bishop in match

indicators.note: exchanging ... for means one letter of the word for youth is swapped out and replaced

parts.note: a minor is a young person, a youth
N is the chess notation for knight
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A young chess player swaps a knight for a bishop during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting makes 'bishop' look like B, but here it is RR, Right Reverend, a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to copy or reflect it exactly, as a looking-glass does, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Where to keep fine tobacco? Small sock should hold enough

indicators.note: should hold means the slang word for enough sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them, to box
'nuff is slang for enough

explanation.surface: Practical advice: keep your fine tobacco in a small sock that holds enough of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock' looks like clothing but is the verb for hitting, giving BOX.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuff is finely powdered tobacco, kept in a small lidded container, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hack into all the same group

indicators.note: into means the word for hack goes inside the word for all the same

parts.note: tho, short for though, means all the same
to hew is to hack or chop

explanation.surface: A journalist joins a group where everyone is identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock band is a musical group, and this is the famous British one.

clue.text: Most expensive type of sword picked up in the streets

indicators.note: in means the reversed sword goes inside the abbreviations for streets

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, so two streets give two of them

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an epee is a type of fencing sword

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a costly sword lying in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' reads the sword word from bottom to top; 'the streets' gives two street abbreviations, one either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for overpriced, so its superlative describes the costliest item.

clue.text: Note about the author inscribed in map of the Underworld

indicators.note: inscribed in means the pieces are written inside the word for map

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
UT is the old name for the note now called doh
on means about, concerning
the author refers to the writer as I

explanation.surface: A musical note and the author's name are written on a chart of Hades.
explanation.walkthrough: UT was the original name for the first note of the scale. 'The author' is the setter speaking of themself, giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was the Roman god of Hades, so the adjective describes anything belonging to his realm.

clue.text: "Utter rubbish" uttered Landau

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Landau is quoted as having said 'Utter rubbish'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' seems part of the quotation but signals the anagram of UTTERED and LANDAU; 'Utter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean complete or total, pure and unmixed, as in absolute nonsense.

clue.text: Middle Earth with another eclipse

indicators.note: with another eclipse means one letter passes in front of the others, so the end letter moves to the start

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes the Earth is midway through a second eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: In an eclipse one body passes in front of another; here the last letter of EARTH moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre or core of something is its middle, as in the heart of the matter.

clue.text: There's no rush to see galleon?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says put ALL in G (good) followed by a word for time, EON, which spells galleon

explanation.surface: No need to hurry to go and see an old sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: G is short for good and an eon is a long time, so the phrase read as instructions builds the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to be patient, as things will happen eventually.

clue.text: It's 3 here, but near midnight perhaps in Washington

definitions.meaning: three is one fourth of twelve, so the number in the clue is described by the phrase
Americans say a ... for 11:45, fifteen minutes before midnight or noon

explanation.surface: A traveller notes it is three o'clock locally but nearly midnight in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like a time-zone difference, but the 3 is arithmetic: one fourth of twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a fourth of twelve, and the US phrasing for 11:45 uses 'of' for 'before'.

clue.text: Debauched cad and roué in a state

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted or depraved, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dissolute scoundrel and a rake are living in a certain country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American country, and a state can mean a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Have some cheese sandwiches — and a small chocolate cake

indicators.note: sandwiches means the cheese wraps around the word for have

parts.note: Brie is a kind of cheese
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: A snack invitation: eat some cheese sandwiches and a little chocolate cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food but is a verb: the cheese encloses the word for have.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense square chocolate bake is a small cake, the standard dictionary sense.

clue.text: British automobile plant

definitions.meaning: the sacred water lily of Asia is this flower

explanation.surface: A British car factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is both a British sports car marque and a water lily.

clue.text: School punishment Arizona's introduced has reduced indolence

indicators.note: introduced means the state abbreviation is put inside the word for the punishment

parts.note: lines are a punishment where a pupil writes out a sentence many times
AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona, the 's meaning is
has shortened to 's leaves just S

explanation.surface: An Arizona school's new detention policy has cut down on idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has reduced' is the contraction 's, giving the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe idleness and an unwillingness to make any effort.

clue.text: Mass is reduced by fusion

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: reduced means the word is is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: X, the multiplication sign, is read as by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A physics statement: mass is lost in nuclear fusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The physics surface hides that 'by' is the times sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend or combination of things joined together is a fusion, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Some hint about becoming a pub landlord?

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gentle hint that someone is about to take over running a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: This jocular old phrase is the traditional way of addressing the innkeeper or publican.

clue.text: An unusual type of cricket?

parts.note: a biological mutant differing from its parent type is called by this name, and cricket is itself a game of that kind

explanation.surface: A naturalist asks about a rare variety of the chirping insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect reading points to biology's term for a mutant; the game reading makes cricket an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A biologist's word for an abnormal mutant, and cricket is an example of a game played competitively.

clue.text: Reading Gaol's new in Twitter?

indicators.note: in means the prison and new go inside the word for twitter

parts.note: birds twitter, that is sing
can is slang for prison, a gaol; the 's is has

explanation.surface: Is a story about Reading Gaol making news on social media?
explanation.walkthrough: Reading Gaol is the prison of Oscar Wilde's ballad; 'Reading' here means looking over text. Twitter is the bird sound, not the website.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickly looking over a text or document is a kind of reading.

clue.text: Aims to get nothing wrong

parts.note: zero means nothing
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone's goal is to make no mistakes at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To home in precisely on a target is to aim at it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Film actor from The Birds makes critical comments

definitions.meaning: Wesley ... is an American film actor
snipe are long-billed wading birds, plural here
to snipe is to criticise in a sly, petty way

explanation.surface: An actor from Hitchcock's The Birds is a harsh critic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birds is Hitchcock's film, but here it simply means some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hollywood actor's surname, a wading bird in plural, and a verb meaning to carp all share one spelling.

clue.text: Police sergeant patrols parts of beach at Qatar? They need minding

indicators.note: patrols means the police abbreviation goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sand is what much of a beach consists of
Q is the international vehicle code for Qatar

explanation.surface: A police officer patrols the sands at a Qatari beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'mind your Ps and Qs' means watch your manners, so they need minding.

clue.text: Depart after tossing firework

indicators.note: after tossing means the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after throwing a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bomb for blowing open gates, the explosive of 'hoist with his own' fame, is loosely a firework.

clue.text: Singing mostly out of tune? Try this register

indicators.note: out of tune means the letters are discordant and rearranged
mostly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A singer is told that, being off-key, they should sign up for lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' suggests a vocal range, but it means to record one's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: To record your arrival in a book or log is to register.

clue.text: It's pleasant to take a long bus ride but __, however

definitions.text: It's pleasant to take a long bus ride but __
definitions.meaning: the blank is filled by ..., i.e. pleasant if you have a seat
however means nevertheless, in spite of that

explanation.surface: A long bus journey is enjoyable, but there is a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer completes the sentence: the ride is pleasant but not when you have to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nevertheless, in spite of what was just said.

clue.text: She emerges from down river occasionally

parts.note: to feel down is to be sad

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A woman appears from downstream now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a particular woman who could be referred to as she.

clue.text: Sadly regrets having ousted leader in East African region

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters are rearranged
having ousted leader means the first letter of the word regrets is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to have deposed a ruler in East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: REGRETS loses its first letter to give EGRETS; with IN and E those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This vast Tanzanian plain famed for wildlife migrations is a region of Africa.
